options: A tool for exporting Prometheus data to a different monitoring system
A small HTTP server that translates a system's native metrics into Prometheus's exposition format
A required component for Prometheus to start up at all
A client library used only for Go applications
questions.explain: An exporter sits in front of something that can't speak Prometheus natively (an OS, a database, a load balancer) and exposes a /metrics endpoint translating its native metrics into Prometheus's text format.

questions.q: What does node_exporter expose metrics about?
options: The internal state of Kubernetes Deployments and Pods
Host/OS-level resources: CPU, memory, disk I/O, network, filesystem usage
Application-specific business metrics like checkout_requests_total
Only Alertmanager's own health
questions.explain: node_exporter runs on or alongside a machine and exposes host-level metrics — CPU, memory, disk, network. It has no visibility into Kubernetes object state or application-specific metrics.

questions.q: What is the purpose of relabeling in Kubernetes service discovery?
options: To rename the Prometheus server itself
To decide which discovered targets to keep or drop, and to rewrite their labels before scraping
To permanently delete time series from the TSDB
To convert gauges into counters
questions.explain: After service discovery finds potential targets with their discovered labels, relabeling rules decide what to keep or drop and can rewrite labels — for example, keeping only pods with a specific annotation and turning a namespace into a clean label.

questions.q: What does kube-state-metrics provide that node_exporter does not?
options: CPU and memory usage per container
The state of Kubernetes objects themselves — like whether a Deployment has its expected number of replicas available
Network latency between pods
PromQL query execution
questions.explain: kube-state-metrics watches the Kubernetes API and exposes the state of Kubernetes objects (Deployments, Pods, etc.) as metrics, which node_exporter — focused purely on machine-level resources — has no visibility into.

questions.q: How would Northbridge make sure Prometheus scrapes only its checkout service's pods, not every pod in the cluster?
options: By manually maintaining a static list of every pod IP address
Using a relabeling rule that keeps only targets carrying a specific scrape annotation
By disabling service discovery entirely
By installing a second Prometheus server for just the checkout namespace
questions.explain: A relabeling rule can filter discovered targets down to only those with a particular annotation (like prometheus.io/scrape: "true"), which is exactly how teams scope scraping to specific services on a shared cluster.
